newsitem.title: DUBAI: Pakistan leaning to Iran gas supplies - paper.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan leaning to Iran gas supplies - paper.

text.p: Pakistan may drop its support for a proposed sub-sea pipeline to import Qatari gas in favour of gas supplies through a land pipeline from Iran, the Dubai-based Gulf News paper reported on Monday.
"As buyers our only concern is economy...and Iran is a better choice," Pakistan Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz was quoted as saying by the paper.
Islamabad had also agreed in principle to Tehran's proposal to extend the pipeline into neighbouring India, Aziz said.
Iran plans to export between eight and 16 billion cubic meters a year of natural gas to Pakistan starting in 2002.
The pipeline project, which is expected to cost $2 billion, is expected to have foreign participation.
Aziz spoke in Gulf Arab Dubai on his way to Iran to attend a Pakistan-Iran Joint Economic Commission meeting which would also discuss a planned joint venture refinery project in Karachi.
